sciatic_n.notes: Actually two nerves (tibial + common fibular divisions) bound in one sheath through the thigh; the split is often already present anatomically well above the knee.

tibial_n.name: Tibial nerve
tibial_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters

common_fibular_n.name: Common fibular (peroneal) nerve
common_fibular_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters
common_fibular_n.notes: Wraps around the fibular neck (superficial, vulnerable to compression/injury -- classic foot-drop mechanism) before dividing into superficial and deep fibular nerves. The short head of biceps femoris is innervated further proximally, by the common-fibular division while still within the sciatic trunk (see sciatic_n targets) -- not by this node itself.

superficial_fibular_n.name: Superficial fibular (peroneal) nerve
superficial_fibular_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters

deep_fibular_n.name: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve
deep_fibular_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters

medial_plantar_n.name: Medial plantar nerve
medial_plantar_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters
medial_plantar_n.notes: The 'median nerve equivalent' of the foot; larger of tibial n.'s two terminal branches.

lateral_plantar_n.name: Lateral plantar nerve
lateral_plantar_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus chapters
lateral_plantar_n.notes: The 'ulnar nerve equivalent' of the foot; deep branch supplies most intrinsic foot muscles.

femoral_n_branch_to_iliacus.name: Femoral n. branch to iliacus
femoral_n_branch_to_iliacus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
femoral_n_branch_to_iliacus.notes: Given off above the inguinal ligament, inside the abdomen. This is why a femoral nerve injury distal to the ligament spares hip flexion by iliacus while abolishing knee extension.

femoral_n_branch_to_pectineus.name: Femoral n. branch to pectineus
femoral_n_branch_to_pectineus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
femoral_n_branch_to_pectineus.notes: Pectineus has a dual supply: femoral nerve, and often an accessory obturator or obturator branch. That dual innervation is the usual explanation for its variable behaviour after isolated nerve injury.

femoral_n_branch_to_sartorius.name: Femoral n. branch to sartorius
femoral_n_branch_to_sartorius.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

femoral_n_branch_to_rectus_femoris.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_lateralis.name: Femoral n. branch to vastus lateralis
femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_lateralis.display_name: Femoral n. branch to vastus lateralis (L2-L4)
femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_lateralis.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_medialis.name: Femoral n. branch to vastus medialis
femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_medialis.display_name: Femoral n. branch to vastus medialis (L2-L4)
femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_medialis.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_medialis.notes: Runs in the adductor canal alongside the saphenous nerve, which is why an adductor canal block placed too proximally can weaken the quadriceps instead of producing the intended purely sensory block.

femoral_n_branch_to_vastus_intermedius.name: Femoral n. branch to vastus intermedius

femoral_n_anterior_cutaneous_branches.name: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve
femoral_n_anterior_cutaneous_branches.display_name: Anterior cutaneous branches of the femoral nerve (L2-L3)
femoral_n_anterior_cutaneous_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the anterior and anteromedial thigh
femoral_n_anterior_cutaneous_branches.notes: Intermediate and medial cutaneous nerves of the thigh; pierce fascia lata to supply the anterior thigh down to the knee.

saphenous_n.name: Saphenous nerve
saphenous_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the anteromedial leg and the medial border of the foot
saphenous_n.notes: The longest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve and its only branch below the knee -- purely sensory. Descends in the adductor (Hunter's) canal, then leaves the canal WITHOUT entering the popliteal fossa, piercing the fascia between sartorius and gracilis. Runs with the great saphenous vein, which makes it the nerve at risk in saphenous vein harvest, varicose vein stripping and medial ankle approaches. The target of the adductor canal block, which spares the quadriceps and so preserves the ability to weight-bear after knee arthroplasty. Course: enters the adductor canal lateral to the femoral artery, crosses anterior to it, and exits through the vasto-adductor membrane roughly a hand's breadth above the knee.

saphenous_n_infrapatellar_branch.name: Infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve
saphenous_n_infrapatellar_branch.display_name: Infrapatellar branch of the saphenous nerve (L3-L4)
saphenous_n_infrapatellar_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin over the patellar tendon and the anteroinferior knee
saphenous_n_infrapatellar_branch.notes: Crosses the front of the knee transversely. Divided by the standard midline knee arthrotomy and by medial arthroscopy portals, producing the numb patch lateral to the scar that many arthroplasty patients report, and occasionally a painful neuroma.

saphenous_n_medial_crural_branches.name: Medial crural cutaneous branches of the saphenous nerve
saphenous_n_medial_crural_branches.display_name: Medial crural cutaneous branches of the saphenous nerve (L3-L4)
saphenous_n_medial_crural_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the medial leg from below the knee to the medial malleolus

obturator_n_anterior_division.name: Obturator n., anterior division
obturator_n_anterior_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
obturator_n_anterior_division.notes: Passes in front of obturator externus and adductor brevis. Supplies the superficial adductor group and gives the cutaneous branch to the medial thigh; also an articular branch to the hip, which is the anatomical basis for hip pathology referring pain to the medial knee (the Obturator/Hilton's law referral).

obturator_n_posterior_division.name: Obturator n., posterior division
obturator_n_posterior_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
obturator_n_posterior_division.notes: Pierces obturator externus and descends behind adductor brevis. Gives an articular branch to the knee through the adductor hiatus -- the other half of the hip-to-knee referral pattern.

obturator_n_branch_to_gracilis.name: Obturator n. branch to gracilis
obturator_n_branch_to_gracilis.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

obturator_n_branch_to_adductor_magnus_ad.name: Obturator n. branch to adductor magnus (adductor part)
obturator_n_branch_to_adductor_magnus_ad.display_name: Obturator n. branch to adductor magnus (adductor part) (L2-L4)
obturator_n_branch_to_adductor_magnus_ad.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
obturator_n_branch_to_adductor_magnus_ad.notes: Adductor magnus is the classic dually innervated muscle: the adductor part is obturator, the ischiocondylar (hamstring) part is the tibial division of the sciatic nerve. The two parts behave as separate functional muscles.

obturator_n_cutaneous_branch.name: Cutaneous branch of the obturator nerve
obturator_n_cutaneous_branch.display_name: Cutaneous branch of the obturator nerve (L2-L4)
obturator_n_cutaneous_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

obturator_n_cutaneous_branch.notes: Small and inconstant; its territory overlaps that of the medial femoral cutaneous branches.

sciatic_n_branch_to_semimembranosus.name: Sciatic n. (tibial division) branch to semimembranosus

sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_long_.name: Sciatic n. (tibial division) branch to biceps femoris, long head
sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_long_.display_name: Sciatic n. (tibial division) branch to biceps femoris, long head (L5-S2)

sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_short.name: Sciatic n. (common fibular division) branch to biceps femoris, short head
sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_short.display_name: Sciatic n. (common fibular division) branch to biceps femoris, short head (L5-S2)
sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_short.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
sciatic_n_branch_to_biceps_femoris_short.notes: The ONLY hamstring supplied by the common fibular division. That makes it a useful electrodiagnostic landmark: short-head denervation with a normal long head localises a lesion to the fibular division rather than the whole sciatic nerve.

tibial_n_branch_to_gastrocnemius.name: Tibial n. branches to gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads)
tibial_n_branch_to_gastrocnemius.display_name: Tibial n. branches to gastrocnemius (medial and lateral heads) (S1-S2)
tibial_n_branch_to_gastrocnemius.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
tibial_n_branch_to_gastrocnemius.notes: Each head receives its own branch, entering close to the popliteal crease. Both heads are common botulinum toxin targets in spastic equinus, and the motor points sit in the proximal third of each belly rather than at its midpoint.

tibial_n_branch_to_soleus.name: Tibial n. branch to soleus
tibial_n_branch_to_soleus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
tibial_n_branch_to_soleus.notes: Soleus usually receives a proximal branch entering its posterior surface near the origin and a second, deeper branch entering the anterior surface further distally, from within the deep posterior compartment. Injection targeting only the superficial belly can therefore miss a substantial part of the muscle.

tibial_n_branch_to_plantaris.name: Tibial n. branch to plantaris
tibial_n_branch_to_plantaris.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

tibial_n_branch_to_popliteus.name: Tibial n. branch to popliteus
tibial_n_branch_to_popliteus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
tibial_n_branch_to_popliteus.notes: Reaches the muscle by winding around its distal border to enter the anterior (deep) surface -- an unusual approach, and one reason popliteus can be spared in some proximal tibial lesions.

tibial_n_branch_to_tibialis_posterior.name: Tibial n. branch to tibialis posterior
tibial_n_branch_to_tibialis_posterior.display_name: Tibial n. branch to tibialis posterior (L4-L5)
tibial_n_branch_to_tibialis_posterior.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
tibial_n_branch_to_tibialis_posterior.notes: A frequent botulinum target in spastic equinovarus, where tibialis posterior drives the varus component. It lies deep, against the interosseous membrane, so accurate injection needs ultrasound or stimulation guidance rather than surface landmarks.

tibial_n_medial_calcaneal_branches.name: Medial calcaneal branches of the tibial nerve

targets: skin of the medial and plantar heel
tibial_n_medial_calcaneal_branches.notes: Arise above or within the tarsal tunnel and pierce the flexor retinaculum. Because they usually branch proximal to the tunnel, heel sensation is often preserved in tarsal tunnel syndrome -- a useful discriminator from plantar fasciitis.

tibial_n_medial_sural_cutaneous_n.name: Medial sural cutaneous nerve
tibial_n_medial_sural_cutaneous_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the posterior leg (upper part)
tibial_n_medial_sural_cutaneous_n.notes: Descends between the two heads of gastrocnemius, then joins the sural communicating branch to form the sural nerve.

common_fibular_n_lateral_sural_cutaneous.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the upper lateral leg

sural_communicating_branch.name: Sural communicating branch
sural_communicating_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
sural_communicating_branch.notes: Its presence and level are variable; in a minority of people it is absent and the sural nerve is formed by the medial sural cutaneous nerve alone.

sural_n.name: Sural nerve
sural_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the posterolateral leg, lateral heel and lateral border of the foot
sural_n.notes: Formed by the medial sural cutaneous nerve joining the sural communicating branch. Runs with the small saphenous vein behind the lateral malleolus. Purely sensory and superficial, which is why it is the standard donor for nerve biopsy and for nerve grafting, and why it is routinely used for sensory conduction studies. Also the nerve at risk in percutaneous Achilles repair and lateral hindfoot approaches.

deep_fibular_n_branch_to_tibialis_anteri.notes: The first muscular branch after the nerve pierces the anterior intermuscular septum. Loss here is the foot drop of a common fibular palsy at the fibular neck.

deep_fibular_n_branch_to_fibularis_terti.notes: Fibularis tertius is absent in a minority of people; when present it is an anterior-compartment muscle and so deep fibular, not superficial fibular, despite its name.

deep_fibular_n_medial_terminal_branch.notes: The first web space is the deep fibular nerve's ONLY cutaneous territory, and is the sensory area tested to separate a deep from a superficial fibular lesion. Entrapment beneath the extensor retinaculum is anterior tarsal tunnel syndrome.

medial_plantar_n_muscular_branches.name: Medial plantar n. muscular branches
medial_plantar_n_muscular_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
medial_plantar_n_muscular_branches.notes: Supplies the first lumbrical only; lumbricals 2-4 are lateral plantar. The pattern mirrors the median/ulnar division of the hand -- medial plantar is the foot's median nerve.

medial_plantar_n_digital_branches.name: Medial plantar n. proper plantar digital nerves
medial_plantar_n_digital_branches.display_name: Medial plantar n. proper plantar digital nerves (S1-S3)
medial_plantar_n_digital_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: plantar skin and nail beds of the medial three and a half toes
medial_plantar_n_digital_branches.notes: The interdigital branches to the second and third web spaces are where Morton's neuroma forms, most often in the third space where medial and lateral plantar branches communicate.

lateral_plantar_n_superficial_branch.name: Lateral plantar n., superficial branch
lateral_plantar_n_superficial_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

lateral_plantar_n_deep_branch.name: Lateral plantar n., deep branch
lateral_plantar_n_deep_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
lateral_plantar_n_deep_branch.notes: Curves medially across the sole with the plantar arch, deep to the long flexor tendons -- the exact counterpart of the deep branch of the ulnar nerve in the hand.

lateral_plantar_n_muscular_branches.name: Lateral plantar n. proximal muscular branches
lateral_plantar_n_muscular_branches.display_name: Lateral plantar n. proximal muscular branches (S1-S3)
lateral_plantar_n_muscular_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- lumbar and sacral plexus sections; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
lateral_plantar_n_muscular_branches.notes: The first branch of the lateral plantar nerve, to abductor digiti minimi, is Baxter's nerve. Its entrapment between abductor hallucis and quadratus plantae is a recognised cause of chronic heel pain that mimics plantar fasciitis but, unlike it, produces no morning-first-step pattern and may show denervation of abductor digiti minimi on EMG.

facial_n_trunk.name: Facial nerve, extracranial trunk
facial_n_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
facial_n_trunk.notes: Exits the stylomastoid foramen and passes through the parotid gland (without supplying it), dividing into 5 terminal branches within the parotid ('pes anserinus').

facial_n_digastric_branch.name: Digastric branch
facial_n_digastric_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

facial_n_cervical_branch.name: Cervical branch

trigeminal_n_v3_trunk.name: Trigeminal n., mandibular division (V3)
trigeminal_n_v3_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v3_trunk.notes: Exits the skull through foramen ovale; the only trigeminal division with a motor root (to the muscles of mastication and other 1st-pharyngeal-arch derivatives).

trigeminal_n_v3_masseteric_branch.name: Masseteric branch
trigeminal_n_v3_masseteric_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigeminal_n_v3_deep_temporal_branches.name: Deep temporal branches
trigeminal_n_v3_deep_temporal_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigeminal_n_v3_medial_pterygoid_branch.name: Medial pterygoid branch
trigeminal_n_v3_medial_pterygoid_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigeminal_n_v3_lateral_pterygoid_branch.name: Lateral pterygoid branch
trigeminal_n_v3_lateral_pterygoid_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

trigeminal_n_v3_mylohyoid_branch.name: Mylohyoid nerve
trigeminal_n_v3_mylohyoid_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v3_mylohyoid_branch.notes: A single branch supplying both mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric -- both derive from the 1st pharyngeal arch, unlike digastric's posterior belly (facial nerve, 2nd arch).

trigeminal_n_v3_tensor_tympani_branch.name: Nerve to tensor tympani
trigeminal_n_v3_tensor_tympani_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: tensor tympani (middle ear muscle, not yet modeled in this pass)

trigeminal_n_v3_tensor_veli_palatini_bra.name: Nerve to tensor veli palatini
trigeminal_n_v3_tensor_veli_palatini_bra.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: tensor veli palatini (soft palate muscle, not yet modeled in this pass)
trigeminal_n_v3_tensor_veli_palatini_bra.notes: Along with tensor tympani, one of the two muscles of pharyngeal-arch-1 origin that are NOT vagus-innervated among the palate/pharynx/larynx muscle group (the classic 'tensor-tensor' exception to the 'everything else is vagus' rule).

oculomotor_n.name: Oculomotor nerve
oculomotor_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
oculomotor_n.notes: Enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure, within the common tendinous ring, dividing into superior and inferior divisions.

oculomotor_n_superior_division.name: Superior division
oculomotor_n_superior_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
oculomotor_n_superior_division.notes: Also supplies levator palpebrae superioris (eyelid elevator, not yet modeled in this pass).

oculomotor_n_inferior_division.name: Inferior division
oculomotor_n_inferior_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
oculomotor_n_inferior_division.notes: Also gives the parasympathetic root to the ciliary ganglion (pupillary sphincter/ciliary muscle -- smooth muscle, out of scope for this skeletal-muscle-focused atlas).

trochlear_n.name: Trochlear nerve
trochlear_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trochlear_n.notes: The only cranial nerve to exit the brainstem dorsally, and the only one supplying a single specific muscle from outside the orbit before entering it.

trochlear_n_terminal.name: Trochlear n. terminal branch
trochlear_n_terminal.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

abducens_n.name: Abducens nerve
abducens_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
abducens_n.notes: Longest intracranial course of any cranial nerve relative to its exit point, making it especially vulnerable to raised intracranial pressure (a classic false-localizing sign).

abducens_n_terminal.name: Abducens n. terminal branch
abducens_n_terminal.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

hypoglossal_n.name: Hypoglossal nerve
hypoglossal_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
hypoglossal_n.notes: Exits the hypoglossal canal of the occipital bone; the C1 ventral ramus fibers that supply geniohyoid and thyrohyoid travel within its sheath for part of its course but are not true CN XII motor fibers (see geniohyoid's documented C1 innervation).

hypoglossal_n_lingual_branches.name: Lingual muscular branches
hypoglossal_n_lingual_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
hypoglossal_n_lingual_branches.notes: Also supplies all intrinsic tongue muscles (not modeled as separate entities in this pass, since they lack discrete bony attachments to anchor a rigid-body compartment).

vagus_n_pharyngeal_contribution.name: Vagus n., pharyngeal plexus contribution
vagus_n_pharyngeal_contribution.display_name: Vagus n., pharyngeal plexus contribution (CN X)
vagus_n_pharyngeal_contribution.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vagus_n_pharyngeal_contribution.notes: The vagus's pharyngeal branches join glossopharyngeal (sensory) and sympathetic fibers on the pharyngeal wall to form the pharyngeal plexus, which supplies essentially all palate/pharynx/larynx muscles except stylopharyngeus (CN IX) and tensor veli palatini (CN V3).

pharyngeal_plexus_to_constrictors.name: Pharyngeal plexus branch to constrictors
pharyngeal_plexus_to_constrictors.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
pharyngeal_plexus_to_constrictors.notes: Also supplies the middle and inferior pharyngeal constrictors (not yet modeled as separate entities in this pass, since the cartilaginous larynx/hyoid-only lower pharynx attachment points are not yet fully skeletonized).

glossopharyngeal_n.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve
glossopharyngeal_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
glossopharyngeal_n.notes: Exits the jugular foramen; the sole exception among pharynx muscles to vagal (pharyngeal plexus) innervation.

glossopharyngeal_n_stylopharyngeus_branc.name: Branch to stylopharyngeus
glossopharyngeal_n_stylopharyngeus_branc.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

cervical_plexus_root_C1.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
cervical_plexus_root_C1.notes: Ventral ramus of spinal nerve C1, contributing to the cervical plexus's loops and branches.

cervical_plexus_root_C2.name: Cervical plexus root, ventral ramus C2

cervical_plexus_root_C3.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
cervical_plexus_root_C3.notes: Ventral ramus of spinal nerve C3, contributing to the cervical plexus's loops and branches.

cervical_plexus_root_C4.notes: Ventral ramus of spinal nerve C4, contributing to the cervical plexus's loops and branches.

ansa_cervicalis_superior_root.name: Ansa cervicalis, superior root (descendens hypoglossi)
ansa_cervicalis_superior_root.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
ansa_cervicalis_superior_root.notes: C1 fibers that join the hypoglossal nerve briefly before leaving it to descend as the superior root of the ansa -- the same C1-via-XII pathway documented in geniohyoid's innervation.

ansa_cervicalis_inferior_root.name: Ansa cervicalis, inferior root (descendens cervicalis)
ansa_cervicalis_inferior_root.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
ansa_cervicalis_inferior_root.notes: Formed from C2-C3 ventral rami; loops down to meet the superior root anterior to the internal/common carotid artery, forming the ansa cervicalis proper. Modeled here with parent_id pointing to the C1 root purely to keep this a valid single-parent tree -- anatomically it is a genuine second, independent contribution (a real loop, not a simple branch), which this schema's parent/child model cannot represent exactly; see module docstring.

ansa_cervicalis_loop.name: Ansa cervicalis (loop)
ansa_cervicalis_loop.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
ansa_cervicalis_loop.notes: The completed loop (C1 superior root + C2-C3 inferior root) gives branches to all the infrahyoid 'strap' muscles except thyrohyoid (which is supplied directly by C1 fibers via the hypoglossal nerve, the same pathway as geniohyoid).

phrenic_n.name: Phrenic nerve
phrenic_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
phrenic_n.notes: The single most clinically important cervical plexus branch; C4 is the major contributor, with C3 and C5 joining the trunk directly from their own cervical plexus roots ('C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive'). A separate, variable accessory phrenic nerve (present in roughly 15-62% of individuals) arises instead from the nerve to subclavius -- a C5 branch of the brachial plexus's upper trunk -- and joins the main phrenic trunk lower in the neck or in the thorax; this accessory pathway is a real but supplemental contribution, not the primary route of the C5 root itself (corrects an earlier draft that conflated the two -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md). Descends through the neck and thorax on scalenus anterior's surface to reach the diaphragm.

phrenic_n_terminal.name: Phrenic n. terminal branches
phrenic_n_terminal.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

cervical_plexus_to_scalenes_and_preverte.name: Cervical plexus muscular branches (scalenes, longus colli)
cervical_plexus_to_scalenes_and_preverte.display_name: Cervical plexus muscular branches (scalenes, longus colli)
cervical_plexus_to_scalenes_and_preverte.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
cervical_plexus_to_scalenes_and_preverte.notes: Segmental branches direct from the cervical plexus roots (C3-C8, the lower contributions overlapping with the brachial plexus) rather than via a single named nerve.

lesser_occipital_n.name: Lesser occipital nerve
lesser_occipital_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin over the lateral scalp posterior to the ear

great_auricular_n.name: Great auricular nerve
great_auricular_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin over the parotid gland and ear
great_auricular_n.notes: Parented to its C2 root; C3's contribution to this and the other C2-C3/C3-C4 cutaneous branches below is a real second root the simple parent/child tree cannot show explicitly (same documented simplification as the ansa cervicalis loop).

transverse_cervical_n.name: Transverse cervical nerve
transverse_cervical_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

supraclavicular_n.name: Supraclavicular nerves
supraclavicular_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

olfactory_n.name: Olfactory nerve (CN I)
olfactory_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: olfactory epithelium of the upper nasal cavity
olfactory_n.notes: Unmyelinated axons of olfactory receptor neurons crossing the cribriform plate of the ethmoid to the olfactory bulb. A CNS tract rather than a true peripheral nerve: no Schwann-cell sheath, and it does not regenerate the way a peripheral nerve does. Sheared by cribriform-plate fracture, causing anosmia.

optic_n.name: Optic nerve (CN II)
optic_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
optic_n.notes: Retinal ganglion cell axons running to the optic chiasm. Also a CNS tract -- myelinated by oligodendrocytes and invested by meninges and subarachnoid space, which is why raised intracranial pressure produces papilloedema.

trigeminal_n_v1_trunk.name: Trigeminal n., ophthalmic division (V1)
trigeminal_n_v1_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v1_trunk.notes: From the trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion in Meckel's cave; runs in the lateral wall of the cavernous sinus and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure. Carries the afferent limb of the corneal reflex, whose efferent limb is CN VII.

trigeminal_n_v1_frontal_branch.name: Frontal nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_frontal_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v1_frontal_branch.notes: Largest V1 branch; runs forward on levator palpebrae superioris and divides into the supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves.

trigeminal_n_v1_supraorbital_branch.name: Supraorbital nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_supraorbital_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the forehead and anterior scalp to the vertex
trigeminal_n_v1_supraorbital_branch.notes: Exits the supraorbital notch or foramen at the medial third of the orbital rim, roughly in line with the pupil in neutral gaze. Supplies forehead and anterior scalp back to the vertex. The standard target for supraorbital nerve block.

trigeminal_n_v1_supratrochlear_branch.name: Supratrochlear nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_supratrochlear_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the medial forehead and upper eyelid
trigeminal_n_v1_supratrochlear_branch.notes: Emerges about a centimetre medial to the supraorbital nerve; supplies the medial forehead and upper eyelid.

trigeminal_n_v1_lacrimal_branch.name: Lacrimal nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_lacrimal_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin and conjunctiva of the lateral upper eyelid
lacrimal gland (secretomotor fibres received via V2)
trigeminal_n_v1_lacrimal_branch.notes: Sensory to the lateral upper eyelid and conjunctiva. Also delivers postganglionic parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the lacrimal gland, which reach it from the zygomatic nerve (V2) through a communicating branch.

trigeminal_n_v1_nasociliary_branch.name: Nasociliary nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_nasociliary_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v1_nasociliary_branch.notes: Gives the long ciliary nerves carrying corneal sensation, the posterior and anterior ethmoidal nerves, and the infratrochlear nerve.

trigeminal_n_v1_anterior_ethmoidal_branc.name: Anterior ethmoidal nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_anterior_ethmoidal_branc.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: mucosa of the anterior nasal septum and lateral wall
skin of the nasal tip (external nasal branch)
trigeminal_n_v1_anterior_ethmoidal_branc.notes: Supplies the anterior nasal septum and lateral wall, then emerges as the external nasal branch to the nasal tip. That territory is the basis of Hutchinson's sign -- vesicles on the nasal tip in herpes zoster ophthalmicus warning of ocular involvement.

trigeminal_n_v1_infratrochlear_branch.name: Infratrochlear nerve
trigeminal_n_v1_infratrochlear_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the medial eyelids, lacrimal sac and side of the nose
trigeminal_n_v1_infratrochlear_branch.notes: Medial eyelids, lacrimal sac and the side of the nose.

trigeminal_n_v2_trunk.name: Trigeminal n., maxillary division (V2)
trigeminal_n_v2_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v2_trunk.notes: Leaves the skull through foramen rotundum, crosses the pterygopalatine fossa, and enters the orbit through the inferior orbital fissure to continue as the infraorbital nerve.

trigeminal_n_v2_infraorbital_branch.name: Infraorbital nerve
trigeminal_n_v2_infraorbital_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the lower eyelid, lateral nose and upper lip
mucosa and gingiva of the upper incisors
trigeminal_n_v2_infraorbital_branch.notes: Emerges from the infraorbital foramen about a centimetre below the orbital rim, vertically in line with the supraorbital notch above and the mental foramen below. Supplies lower eyelid, lateral nose, upper lip and upper incisor gingiva. Injured in orbital floor blow-out fracture.

trigeminal_n_v2_superior_alveolar_branch.name: Superior alveolar nerves (anterior, middle, posterior)
trigeminal_n_v2_superior_alveolar_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: mucosal lining of the maxillary sinus
trigeminal_n_v2_superior_alveolar_branch.notes: Form the superior dental plexus supplying the maxillary teeth and the lining of the maxillary sinus -- which is why maxillary sinusitis so often presents as upper molar toothache.

trigeminal_n_v2_zygomatic_branch.name: Zygomatic nerve (zygomaticotemporal + zygomaticofacial)
trigeminal_n_v2_zygomatic_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin over the temple and the prominence of the cheek
trigeminal_n_v2_zygomatic_branch.notes: Sensory to the temple and the prominence of the cheek. Carries the parasympathetic fibres destined for the lacrimal gland and hands them to the lacrimal nerve of V1.

trigeminal_n_v2_palatine_branches.name: Nasopalatine and greater/lesser palatine nerves
trigeminal_n_v2_palatine_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: mucosa of the hard and soft palate
trigeminal_n_v2_palatine_branches.notes: Distributed from the pterygopalatine ganglion to the nasal septum and to the hard and soft palate mucosa.

trigeminal_n_v3_auriculotemporal_branch.name: Auriculotemporal nerve
trigeminal_n_v3_auriculotemporal_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the temple, external acoustic meatus and tympanic membrane
parotid gland (secretomotor fibres from the otic ganglion)
trigeminal_n_v3_auriculotemporal_branch.notes: Encircles the middle meningeal artery by two roots, passes behind the temporomandibular joint and ascends with the superficial temporal vessels. Sensory to the TMJ, external acoustic meatus, tympanic membrane and temple, and it carries secretomotor fibres to the parotid from the otic ganglion. That parotid course underlies Frey syndrome after parotidectomy, and its TMJ supply is why joint pathology refers pain to the ear.

trigeminal_n_v3_inferior_alveolar_branch.name: Inferior alveolar nerve
trigeminal_n_v3_inferior_alveolar_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
trigeminal_n_v3_inferior_alveolar_branch.notes: Enters the mandibular foramen, runs the mandibular canal supplying the lower teeth, and leaves as the mental nerve. Target of the standard inferior alveolar dental block, and the nerve at risk in third-molar extraction and mandibular angle fracture.

trigeminal_n_v3_mental_branch.name: Mental nerve
trigeminal_n_v3_mental_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin of the chin and lower lip
trigeminal_n_v3_mental_branch.notes: Exits the mental foramen, usually near the lower premolar roots, completing the vertical line of supraorbital, infraorbital and mental foramina. Supplies the chin and lower lip.

trigeminal_n_v3_buccal_branch.name: Buccal nerve (sensory, V3)
trigeminal_n_v3_buccal_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: skin and mucosa of the cheek
trigeminal_n_v3_buccal_branch.notes: Sensory to cheek mucosa and skin. Not to be confused with the buccal BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE, which is motor to buccinator: the muscle is CN VII, the sensation over it is V3.

trigeminal_n_v3_lingual_branch.name: Lingual nerve
trigeminal_n_v3_lingual_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: mucosa of the anterior two-thirds of the tongue (general sensation)
floor of the mouth and lingual gingiva
trigeminal_n_v3_lingual_branch.notes: General sensation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, and the conduit for chorda tympani (CN VII) fibres carrying taste and submandibular/sublingual secretomotor supply. Lies directly deep to the mucosa beside the third molar, where it is vulnerable during extraction.

vestibulocochlear_n.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)
vestibulocochlear_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vestibulocochlear_n.notes: Traverses the internal acoustic meatus alongside CN VII. Site of vestibular schwannoma, which characteristically presents with unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus before vertigo, because central compensation masks slowly progressive vestibular loss.

vestibulocochlear_n_cochlear_division.name: Cochlear division (CN VIII)
vestibulocochlear_n_cochlear_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vestibulocochlear_n_cochlear_division.notes: Bipolar neurons of the spiral ganglion; hearing.

vestibulocochlear_n_vestibular_division.name: Vestibular division (CN VIII)
vestibulocochlear_n_vestibular_division.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: semicircular canal cristae, utricular and saccular maculae
vestibulocochlear_n_vestibular_division.notes: Superior and inferior divisions arising from the vestibular (Scarpa's) ganglion, serving the semicircular canals, utricle and saccule.

accessory_n.name: Accessory nerve (CN XI), spinal root
accessory_n.display_name: Accessory nerve (CN XI), spinal root (C1-C5/C6 spinal accessory nucleus)
accessory_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
accessory_n.notes: Ascends through the foramen magnum, leaves by the jugular foramen, then descends across the posterior triangle of the neck. In that triangle it lies SUBCUTANEOUSLY, crossing at about the junction of the upper and middle thirds of the posterior border of sternocleidomastoid. It is the most commonly iatrogenically injured nerve of the neck -- typically during posterior triangle lymph node biopsy -- producing trapezius palsy with shoulder droop, lateral scapular winging and painful loss of abduction above 90 degrees.

accessory_n_scm_branch.name: Accessory n. branch to sternocleidomastoid
accessory_n_scm_branch.root_contributions: C1-C3, with a cervical plexus contribution
accessory_n_scm_branch.display_name: Accessory n. branch to sternocleidomastoid (C1-C3, with a cervical plexus contribution)
accessory_n_scm_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

accessory_n_trapezius_branch.name: Accessory n. branch to trapezius
accessory_n_trapezius_branch.root_contributions: motor from the spinal accessory nucleus; C3-C4 adds proprioceptive/sensory fibres
accessory_n_trapezius_branch.display_name: Accessory n. branch to trapezius (motor from the spinal accessory nucleus; C3-C4 adds proprioceptive/sensory fibres)
accessory_n_trapezius_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

vagus_n_trunk.name: Vagus nerve (CN X), cervical trunk
vagus_n_trunk.root_contributions: dorsal motor nucleus, nucleus ambiguus, nucleus of the solitary tract
vagus_n_trunk.display_name: Vagus nerve (CN X), cervical trunk (dorsal motor nucleus, nucleus ambiguus, nucleus of the solitary tract)
vagus_n_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vagus_n_trunk.notes: Descends inside the carotid sheath, between and behind the internal jugular vein and the common carotid artery. The longest cranial nerve; mixed motor, sensory and parasympathetic.

vagus_n_superior_laryngeal_branch.name: Superior laryngeal nerve
vagus_n_superior_laryngeal_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: laryngeal mucosa above the vocal folds (internal branch)
vagus_n_superior_laryngeal_branch.notes: Divides into an internal branch -- sensory above the vocal folds, the afferent limb of the cough reflex, piercing the thyrohyoid membrane -- and an external branch, motor to cricothyroid. The external branch runs with the superior thyroid artery and is at risk in thyroidectomy; injury lowers vocal pitch and weakens projection without causing frank hoarseness.

vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_r.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, right
vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_r.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: laryngeal mucosa below the vocal folds
vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_r.notes: Hooks beneath the RIGHT SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY and ascends in the tracheo-oesophageal groove. Shorter and more oblique than the left, and more variable -- including a non-recurrent variant associated with an aberrant right subclavian artery, which raises operative risk precisely because the nerve is not where it is expected.

vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_l.name: Recurrent laryngeal nerve, left
vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_l.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: laryngeal mucosa below the vocal folds
vagus_n_recurrent_laryngeal_branch_l.notes: Hooks beneath the AORTIC ARCH lateral to the ligamentum arteriosum, giving it a long intrathoracic course. This is why left vocal cord palsy is a recognised presenting sign of mediastinal pathology -- lung apex tumour, aortic arch aneurysm, left atrial enlargement. Both recurrent laryngeal nerves supply every intrinsic laryngeal muscle except cricothyroid. Targets corrected: this branch had been given the RIGHT laryngeal compartments, so the left recurrent laryngeal nerve appeared to supply the right larynx and nothing reached the left.

vagus_n_cardiac_branches.name: Vagal cardiac branches (cervical and thoracic)
vagus_n_cardiac_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed. -- head and neck / summary of cranial nerves; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vagus_n_cardiac_branches.notes: Parasympathetic supply to the cardiac plexus; the efferent limb of the baroreceptor reflex, and the pathway exploited by vagal manoeuvres used to terminate supraventricular tachycardia.

vagus_n_oesophageal_trunk.name: Vagus n., oesophageal (thoracic) trunk
vagus_n_oesophageal_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.4 'Thorax'; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
vagus_n_oesophageal_trunk.notes: Q265: added this round (Q261 had flagged real targets -- zan_oesophagus, zan_stomach, lung meshes -- but no registry node yet). Below the roots of the lungs each vagus breaks up into several rami that re-form a plexus directly on the oesophagus's own surface (the oesophageal plexus), continuing down to the diaphragm; this atlas represents the whole plexus, per side, as one continuing round tube along the real oesophagus's own surface rather than modelling the individual rami, stated as a simplification.

vagus_n_abdominal_trunk.name: Vagus n., abdominal (anterior/posterior) trunk
vagus_n_abdominal_trunk.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.5 'Abdomen'; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: stomach (lesser/greater curvature, near the oesophagogastric junction)
vagus_n_abdominal_trunk.notes: Q265: at the oesophageal hiatus the periesophageal plexus re-condenses into a predominantly-left ANTERIOR vagal trunk (on the stomach's anterior surface) and a predominantly-right POSTERIOR vagal trunk (posterior surface) -- a real, well-documented left/right asymmetry this atlas does not re-derive (no fibre-tracing data exists in any source file here); represented honestly as each side's own trunk continuing to its own nearest real stomach surface, not literally crossing to the opposite side.

vagus_n_coeliac_branch.name: Vagus n., coeliac branch (posterior trunk)
vagus_n_coeliac_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.5 'Abdomen'; Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: coeliac plexus (around the coeliac trunk's origin from the aorta)
vagus_n_coeliac_branch.notes: Q265: the posterior vagal trunk's major coeliac branch, joining the coeliac plexus/ganglia that also receive the greater splanchnic nerve (already built, Q259) -- same coeliac-trunk-origin target and the same own-page abdominal-aorta proxy Q259 already established and cites, reused here rather than re-derived.

glossopharyngeal_n_tympanic_branch.name: Tympanic branch (nerve of Jacobson)
glossopharyngeal_n_tympanic_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
glossopharyngeal_n_tympanic_branch.notes: Re-enters the temporal bone through the inferior tympanic canaliculus to form the tympanic plexus on the promontory of the middle ear, then continues as the lesser petrosal nerve -- the parasympathetic route to the otic ganglion and, from there, the parotid gland.

lesser_petrosal_n.name: Lesser petrosal nerve
lesser_petrosal_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
lesser_petrosal_n.notes: Carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the tympanic plexus to the otic ganglion, exiting the skull through the foramen ovale alongside the mandibular nerve (CN V3).

glossopharyngeal_n_carotid_branch.name: Carotid sinus branch
glossopharyngeal_n_carotid_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: carotid sinus baroreceptors and carotid body chemoreceptors -- the afferent limb of the baroreceptor reflex; also at risk in carotid endarterectomy, where inadvertent stimulation causes acute bradycardia and hypotension

glossopharyngeal_n_tonsillar_branches.name: Tonsillar branches
glossopharyngeal_n_tonsillar_branches.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: palatine tonsil and surrounding oropharyngeal mucosa (soft palate, fauces) -- the sensory territory numbed by a peritonsillar/glossopharyngeal nerve block for tonsillectomy or awake fiberoptic intubation

glossopharyngeal_n_lingual_branch.name: Lingual branches
glossopharyngeal_n_lingual_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: general sensation and taste from the posterior third of the tongue and vallate papillae -- the reason posterior tongue lesions refer pain to the ear (via the tympanic branch's shared central connections), unlike anterior two-thirds lesions

otic_ganglion.name: Otic ganglion
otic_ganglion.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: parotid gland (secretomotor) -- the parasympathetic supply responsible for salivation; aberrant regeneration of these fibers onto sweat glands after parotid surgery, misdirected to the overlying skin, produces Frey's (gustatory sweating) syndrome
otic_ganglion.notes: Lies just below the foramen ovale, applied to the mandibular nerve; postganglionic fibers reach the parotid gland by hitching a ride on the auriculotemporal nerve (CN V3) rather than traveling independently.

greater_petrosal_n.name: Greater petrosal nerve
greater_petrosal_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
greater_petrosal_n.notes: Arises from the facial nerve at the geniculate ganglion, inside the temporal bone -- proximal to the stylomastoid foramen this atlas's facial_n_trunk otherwise starts from, included here as a child of it for parasympathetic completeness. Joins the deep petrosal (sympathetic) nerve to form the nerve of the pterygoid canal, which reaches the pterygopalatine ganglion.

pterygopalatine_ganglion.name: Pterygopalatine (sphenopalatine) ganglion
pterygopalatine_ganglion.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Piagkou M et al., Pain Pract 12:399 (2012) [SPG block anatomy]
targets: lacrimal gland (via the zygomatic nerve and lacrimal nerve, a well-documented parasympathetic detour through two branches of CN V1/V2) and the mucous glands of the nasal cavity, palate and pharynx
pterygopalatine_ganglion.notes: The largest of the four cranial parasympathetic ganglia, suspended in the pterygopalatine fossa. Reached transnasally for sphenopalatine ganglion (SPG) block, a real image-guided/topical procedure used for cluster headache, migraine, and some facial neuralgias -- one of the few parasympathetic ganglia that is itself a routine injection/block target rather than only a relay point.

chorda_tympani_n.name: Chorda tympani
chorda_tympani_n.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
chorda_tympani_n.notes: Branches from the facial nerve in the facial canal, proximal to the stylomastoid foramen -- like the greater petrosal nerve, included here as a child of facial_n_trunk for parasympathetic completeness. Crosses the middle ear medial to the tympanic membrane (at risk in middle-ear surgery), then joins the lingual nerve (CN V3) to travel with it to the submandibular ganglion.

submandibular_ganglion.name: Submandibular ganglion
submandibular_ganglion.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: submandibular and sublingual salivary glands (secretomotor); also carries taste fibers from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue, via the chorda tympani and lingual nerve, through this same relay without synapsing
submandibular_ganglion.notes: Suspended from the lingual nerve above the deep part of the submandibular gland -- the only cranial parasympathetic ganglion not applied directly to a named foramen, since it hangs from the nerve carrying its preganglionic fibers rather than sitting at their site of entry.

ciliary_ganglion.name: Ciliary ganglion
ciliary_ganglion.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: sphincter pupillae (pupillary constriction) and ciliary muscle (lens accommodation) -- both smooth muscle, not modeled as discrete entities in this atlas; postganglionic fibers reach the globe as the short ciliary nerves
ciliary_ganglion.notes: The smallest of the four cranial parasympathetic ganglia, lying in the posterior orbit between the optic nerve and lateral rectus. Receives its parasympathetic root from the branch to inferior oblique (part of the oculomotor nerve's inferior division); a lesion here or along that root -- compressive (uncal herniation) or pharmacologic (mydriatic drops) -- produces a fixed, dilated pupil (Adie's tonic pupil, when the lesion is the ciliary ganglion itself) before it produces any extraocular muscle weakness, because the pupillomotor fibers run on the nerve's outer surface.

facial_n_posterior_auricular_branch.name: Posterior auricular branch
facial_n_posterior_auricular_branch.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998). Added 2026-09-14 (Q65) with the auricular muscles.

superior_cervical_ganglion_r.name: Superior cervical ganglion
superior_cervical_ganglion_r.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
superior_cervical_ganglion_r.notes: The largest and most cephalad ganglion of the sympathetic trunk, lying behind the internal carotid artery at the C1-C2 level. Receives preganglionic fibers that have ascended from the upper thoracic cord without synapsing; every postganglionic fiber reaching the head originates here.

superior_cervical_ganglion_l.name: Superior cervical ganglion

superior_cervical_ganglion_l.notes: The largest and most cephalad ganglion of the sympathetic trunk, lying behind the internal carotid artery at the C1-C2 level. internal_carotid_nerve_r.name: Internal carotid nerve
internal_carotid_nerve_r.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

stellate_ganglion_r.name: Stellate (cervicothoracic) ganglion
stellate_ganglion_r.root_contributions: C8-T1 (fused inferior cervical and first thoracic ganglia)
stellate_ganglion_r.display_name: Stellate (cervicothoracic) ganglion (C8-T1 (fused inferior cervical and first thoracic ganglia))

stellate_ganglion_r.notes: Lies anterior to the C7 transverse process and the neck of the first rib, just posterior to the vertebral artery's origin -- the reason ultrasound guidance (targeting the C6 tubercle or C7 level, avoiding the vertebral artery) has largely replaced the blind anterior paratracheal approach for stellate ganglion block, used for complex regional pain syndrome of the upper limb, refractory angina, and some vascular insufficiency syndromes. A successful block reproduces Horner's syndrome, which is the clinical proof the block reached its target rather than evidence of a complication.

greater_splanchnic_n_r.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
greater_splanchnic_n_r.notes: Pierces the diaphragmatic crus to reach the abdomen, carrying preganglionic fibers that do not synapse until the celiac ganglion -- this is why splanchnic and celiac plexus neurolysis (for pancreatic cancer pain) target the same functional pathway from two different levels.

greater_splanchnic_n_l.name: Greater splanchnic nerve

lumbar_sympathetic_chain_r.root_contributions: L1-L5 (typically 4 paravertebral ganglia, modeled as one chain entry)
lumbar_sympathetic_chain_r.display_name: Lumbar sympathetic chain (L1-L5 (typically 4 paravertebral ganglia, modeled as one chain entry))

lumbar_sympathetic_chain_r.notes: Runs along the anterolateral border of the vertebral bodies, medial to psoas major -- the needle path for a lumbar sympathetic block passes through or just anterior to psoas, which is what separates this block from a psoas compartment (lumbar plexus) block done from the same posterior approach at a similar depth. ganglion_impar.name: Ganglion impar (of Walther)
ganglion_impar.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Oh CS et al., Reg Anesth Pain Med 29:270 (2004) [ganglion impar block technique]
targets: sympathetic and visceral afferent fibers to the coccyx, perineum, distal rectum, and anus -- a terminal midline relay, not a named end-organ
ganglion_impar.notes: The single midline terminus where both sacral sympathetic chains fuse, anterior to the sacrococcygeal joint. Modeled here as a child of the right chain alone; it is anatomically the meeting point of both. Its block (transsacrococcygeal or paracoccygeal approach) treats coccydynia and other sympathetically mediated perineal/anorectal pain, and is one of the few midline neuraxial-adjacent targets reached from directly behind the coccyx.

celiac_plexus.name: Celiac plexus (solar plexus)
celiac_plexus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Malfertheiner P et al. (celiac plexus neurolysis literature, general reference)
targets: stomach, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and small and large bowel to the splenic flexure -- essentially all foregut and midgut viscera, via the subsidiary hepatic, splenic, superior mesenteric and renal plexuses
celiac_plexus.notes: The largest prevertebral autonomic plexus, surrounding the celiac trunk's origin from the aorta at approximately T12-L1, flanked by the paired celiac ganglia. Receives the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves bilaterally and both vagal trunks -- modeled here as a child of the right greater splanchnic nerve alone as a tree-structure simplification. Celiac plexus block/neurolysis (percutaneous retrocrural, anterior transabdominal, or endoscopic-ultrasound-guided) treats pain from pancreatic and other upper-abdominal malignancy by interrupting visceral afferents before they reach the cord.

superior_hypogastric_plexus.name: Superior hypogastric plexus
superior_hypogastric_plexus.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Plancarte R et al., Anesthesiology 73:236 (1990) [superior hypogastric plexus block technique]
superior_hypogastric_plexus.notes: Lies anterior to the L5-S1 disc and sacral promontory, continuing the aortic plexus inferiorly before dividing into the two hypogastric nerves that carry sympathetic (and mixed) fibers down to the pelvic (inferior hypogastric) plexuses. Its block treats pelvic cancer pain and some chronic pelvic pain syndromes, approached posterolaterally at the L4-L5 level to reach anterior to the sacral promontory.

inferior_hypogastric_plexus_r.name: Inferior hypogastric (pelvic) plexus
inferior_hypogastric_plexus_r.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
targets: bladder, rectum, and (uterus and vagina, or prostate and seminal vesicles) via the vesical, middle/inferior rectal, and uterovaginal or prostatic nerve subplexuses; also the corpora cavernosa/clitoris via the cavernous nerves, making this plexus the anatomical basis of pelvic organ and erectile innervation
inferior_hypogastric_plexus_r.notes: Lies against the lateral pelvic wall alongside the internal iliac vessels, receiving sympathetic input from the hypogastric nerve and parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) in the same plexus -- one of the few points in the body where sympathetic and parasympathetic fibers share a single named plexus before diverging to their end organs.
